fields.description:
## Report

The Gerrit LLM-Review bot does not reliably queue a review when a patch set is uploaded. The change sits with `LLM-Review = --` indefinitely, and only starts reviewing after a human/agent posts a `recheck-review` comment or force-pushes a no-op rebase.

## Evidence — four reproductions, 2026-08-07

1. **Change 1486 (599e):** both patch-set uploads skipped; needed a `recheck-review` comment to queue.
2. **Change 1490 (e7a9):** no vote on upload. `recheck-review` at 11:41 -> `LLM-Review -1` at 11:44. Healthy and fast ONCE TRIGGERED.
3. **Changes 1493 / 1496 (13b4, ccf6):** both skipped; 1493 sat 70 minutes unvoted while the bot voted on NEWER changes (1497) in the same window. A no-op rebase + re-push produced votes within 5 minutes on both.
4. **Fleet-level:** at ~11:50, `LLM-Review = --` on 1486, 1488, 1491, 1492, 1493, 1494, 1495 simultaneously while `Verified` votes landed normally.

Second-order cost: it is INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM AN OUTAGE. The e7a9 agent concluded "the reviewer looks down" and STOPPED work on a completed, correct change that had in fact already been reviewed.

## ROOT CAUSE (proven — see the RCA comment for the full experiment log)

`reconcile_once` (`src/rebar/review_bot/reconcile.py:232-235`) writes its persisted cursor to `newest` — the max event time across the WHOLE fetched window — **unconditionally at the end of every pass**, with no low-water mark for candidates the pass failed to vote. Three paths `continue` without voting: `reconcile_check_error` (`:213`), `review_timeout` (`:227-228`), and a voter `deferred`/`error` return. Because the events-log `?t1=` window filters SERVER-SIDE (proven live: `t1=13:00:00` returns `oldest=13:00:18`), those events are excluded from every future window — permanently.

Since Gerrit's `webhooks` plugin is at-**most**-once (plugin `PostTask.run()` logs SEVERE and discards after `maxTries`; contradicting the "at-least-once" claim at `docs/adr/0009-review-bot-pipe.md:82`) and the receiver 202-ACKs into an in-memory queue that a container recreation discards (`app.py:112`, `:135-143`), the reconciler is the ONLY recovery path — and it blinds itself.

Runtime proof (3 passes, fake events-log honouring `since`, middle candidate times out):
```
PASS 1: window=[Iaaa,Ibbb,Iccc] result={scanned:2,reviewed:1} cursor=10:53:50
PASS 2: window=[Iccc]           result={scanned:0,reviewed:0} cursor=10:53:50
PASS 3: window=[Iccc]           result={scanned:0,reviewed:0} cursor=10:53:50
```

This is why BOTH nudges work: each mints a NEW events-log event AFTER the cursor, re-admitting the change to the window. Nothing else does.

Contracts violated: `reconcile.py:1-10` ("This poller closes that loop"), `reconcile.py:218-220` ("is retried next pass"), `docs/adr/0009-review-bot-pipe.md:111` ("the reconciler is what recovers a dropped webhook"), `docs/review-policy.md:65` ("re-drives it automatically within its interval").

Why it shipped: the guarding test double records `since` and then ignores it (`tests/unit/test_review_bot.py:682-687`), so the production cursor filter is never exercised by `test_deferred_change_stays_eligible_for_reconciler` (`:1878`) or `test_reconcile_once_times_out_a_hung_review_and_continues` (`:1392`).

## Fix plan

### Step 1 — `src/rebar/review_bot/reconcile.py`: cursor low-water mark (the root-cause fix)

Track the oldest event time among candidates the pass did NOT reach a TERMINAL outcome for, and clamp the persisted cursor to strictly before that time, so those candidates re-enter the next window and are re-driven — exactly as `reconcile.py:1-10` and `:218-220` already promise.

**The partition is explicit, over the voter's actual status vocabulary** (`src/rebar/review_bot/voter.py`), because "not voted" and "retryable" are NOT the same set:

| outcome | source | cursor |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `voted` | `voter.py:773` | **ADVANCE** — done |
| `skipped`/`malformed_event` | `voter.py:493` | **ADVANCE** — terminal, re-driving cannot help |
| `skipped`/`other_project` | `voter.py:503` | **ADVANCE** — terminal, never ours |
| `skipped`/`dedup` | `voter.py:527` | **ADVANCE** — already voted |
| `skipped`/`already_voted_gerrit` | `voter.py:540` | **ADVANCE** — already voted |
| `skipped`/`post_vote_closed` | `voter.py:715` | **ADVANCE** — change merged/abandoned mid-review; it is unvotable and a re-drive would 409 forever (bug c943) |
| `error` (`dedup_check`, `review_setup`, `post_vote`, tree-mismatch) | `voter.py:552, 621, 636, 725` | **HOLD** — transient, retryable |
| `deferred` | `voter.py:672` | **HOLD** — the retryable coverage gap that `voter.py:638-641` explicitly contracts on the reconciler re-driving |
| `reconcile_check_error` | `reconcile.py:213` | **HOLD** — transient Gerrit read failure |
| `review_timeout` | `reconcile.py:227-228` | **HOLD** — `app.py:198-205` and `reconcile.py:218-220` both promise a reconciler retry |

Worked example (three candidates in one window; A at t=10 times out, B at t=20 votes, unrelated `comment-added` at t=30):
* today — cursor := 30; A is outside every future window; A is **never** voted.
* after the fix — low-water := 10, cursor := 9; next pass re-fetches A and B; B short-circuits on `already_voted` (`voter.py:519`) and A is re-driven.

**Bounded hold-back (poison-pill guard).** A candidate that fails on EVERY pass would otherwise pin the cursor forever and grow the fetch window without bound. Cap the hold-back: the cursor is never clamped more than `RECONCILE_MAX_HOLDBACK_SECONDS` (new config key, default 86400) behind `newest`. Past that ceiling the cursor advances, the candidate is released, and it is emitted as a distinct `RECONCILE_DEGRADED` reason (`holdback_expired`) so a chronically-stuck change is surfaced loudly rather than silently retried forever.

Idempotency is unchanged: the dedup ledger plus the authoritative Gerrit `has_llm_review_vote` pre-filter (`reconcile.py:207-215`) still make a re-drive a no-op once a vote exists, so the fix can only ADD recovery, never a double vote.

### Step 2 — `src/rebar/review_bot/reconcile.py`: make the abandonment observable

`reconcile_done` reports only `scanned`/`reviewed`. Add `held_back` (count of candidates the pass left un-voted and will re-drive) and `cursor` (the value actually persisted), so "backfill is carrying N stalled changes, pinned at T" is greppable instead of silent.

### Step 3 — `src/rebar/review_bot/app.py`: expose queue depth on `/health` (AC5)

`/health` reports only `in_flight`, so an agent cannot distinguish "not queued" from "queued behind N" from "bot down". Add `queue_depth` (the live `asyncio.Queue.qsize()`) alongside `in_flight`, following the precedent that field already set as a load-bearing observable for the autodeploy drain (bug 34cd, `app.py:245-263`). Existing keys are unchanged, so every current caller keeps working.

### Step 4 — `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py`: repair the false green and add the RED tests

1. Make the fake `list_events` HONOUR `since` (`tests/unit/test_review_bot.py:682-687` currently records it and returns the full list), matching the proven live semantics — an inclusive, server-side lower bound.
2. Add a multi-event-window regression test: three events, the NON-newest candidate's review times out, assert pass 2's window still contains it and it is re-driven. This is the test the current double cannot express and is why the defect shipped.
3. Add a terminal-outcome test: a `skipped`/`post_vote_closed` candidate must NOT pin the cursor (guards the partition above).
4. Add a hold-back-ceiling test: a candidate failing repeatedly is released once `RECONCILE_MAX_HOLDBACK_SECONDS` elapses, and emits `holdback_expired`.
5. Add an AC5 test: with N events queued, `GET /health` returns `queue_depth == N` alongside `in_flight`.
6. Assert `recheck-review` still queues a review after the change (AC4's measurable half).

### Step 5 — `docs/adr/0009-review-bot-pipe.md`: correct the false delivery premise

`docs/adr/0009-review-bot-pipe.md:82` (echoed at `src/rebar/review_bot/dedup.py:3-5`) asserts the Gerrit `webhooks` plugin *"delivers at-least-once"*. The plugin source (`PostTask.run()`) logs SEVERE and DISCARDS after `maxTries`, retries only non-SSL `IOException`, and loses pending deliveries on restart — it is at-**most**-once. Correct both statements, because the whole "ACK fast into an in-memory queue is safe" argument rests on that sentence being true.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Root cause established for why the upload event does not queue a review — proven, not inferred (runtime experiment + live events-log probe; see RCA comment)
- [ ] A patch-set upload that the webhook drops is re-driven WITHOUT any manual comment. Verified by `pytest tests/unit/test_review_bot.py -k reconcile_cursor` — two reconcile passes against a `since`-honouring events-log; the un-voted, NON-newest candidate is re-driven on pass 2.
- [ ] A terminal outcome does NOT pin the cursor. Verified by the `post_vote_closed` case in the same test module: the persisted cursor advances past it.
- [ ] A chronically-failing candidate cannot pin the window forever. Verified by the hold-back-ceiling test: past `RECONCILE_MAX_HOLDBACK_SECONDS` the cursor advances and `RECONCILE_DEGRADED reason=holdback_expired` is emitted.
- [ ] Backfill's carried backlog is OBSERVABLE. Verified by asserting `reconcile_done` emits `held_back` and `cursor`.
- [ ] `recheck-review` remains available as a manual override. Verified by asserting a `recheck-review` comment still queues a review after this change.
- [ ] 'not queued' vs 'queued behind N' vs 'running' is visible. Verified by a test that queues N events and asserts `GET /health` returns `queue_depth == N` alongside `in_flight`.
- [ ] `docs/adr/0009-review-bot-pipe.md:82` no longer claims the webhooks plugin delivers at-least-once.
